description: Un equipo de futuros geólogos que buscan hacer un cambio a un nivel espacial.
summary: Abandoned but not Forgotten is a bilingual (English/Spanish) interactive learning app that tells the story of 11 NASA explorers, from Surveyor 3 (1967) to Perseverance (2026). Students fly through a 3D atlas of the Solar System, the Moon and Mars, scrub through time, and open each machine to see real NASA photos, its NASA ID and date, its instrument and a short science explanation. It answers the challenge by turning discarded and still-active NASA equipment into stories that school-age space enthusiasts can explore and play with. It matters because these machines often worked far longer than planned and taught us about the Moon, Mars and deep space, and their stories deserve to be remembered.
details:
CHALLENGE: Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars. Audience: school-age space enthusiasts.

WHAT IT DOES

The app covers 11 NASA objects. Seven are inactive: Surveyor 3, the three Apollo Lunar Rovers (Apollo 15, 16 and 17, counted as one entry), Viking 1, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and Ingenuity. Four are still active in 2026: Voyager 2, New Horizons, Curiosity and Perseverance.

HOW IT WORKS

- A 3D atlas of the Solar System, the Moon and Mars, with a 3D model of each machine.

- A time slider (1967 to 2026) with Play, speed controls and milestone buttons.

- Clicking a machine opens a window with real NASA photos, the NASA ID and date, the instrument, and a short science explanation.

- A bar chart compares planned lifetime with real lifetime for 9 missions.

- A time-travel ordering game and a 12-question mission quiz help students check what they learned.

- The whole app switches between English and Spanish.

BENEFITS

Students see where each machine is, when it worked, and what science it made possible, using real NASA imagery and data. The planned-vs-real chart shows how engineering often exceeds its goals. The app is free, runs in a browser and is available in two languages.

GOALS

We hope to make the history of space exploration approachable for young people, and to show that machines that have gone silent still teach us about the Moon and Mars.

TOOLS

Web application developed with Google AI Studio. Real NASA photographs come live from the NASA Image and Video Library API; 3D textures come from NASA SVS and USGS data. Fonts: Fira Sans and Overpass (Google Fonts).

TEAM

Team Geólogos FC, a team of future geologists who want to make an impact at a space level: Anthony Luna Carvajal, Roberth Torres Hernández, Lady Thayris Valle Gadea and Alejandro Miguel Fuentes Brenes. NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, San José, Costa Rica.
